_comment: SYNTHETIC SAMPLE. Every number below is invented - this file documents the format check-segment-efforts.mjs reads, nothing more. The real set is segment-efforts.json, which is gitignored and never enters the repo (see README.md, 'Where the data lives'). Build it locally with add-segment-effort.mjs.
source: Strava segment efforts on Zwift route laps - exact distance, exact time, no lead-in.
privacy: No athlete, activity title or activity id is stored. A record is a route, a distance, a time, a power and the rider's weight and height, which is all the physics consumes.
why: A segment starts and ends at fixed points, so an event pen cannot inflate it and riding past the finish line cannot either. That makes one effort a stronger test than a whole field whose ridden distance had to be inferred - see docs/race-drafting.md §5, 'What sand turned out not to be'.
columns: routeSlug (catalog slug, numeric id for routes zwift-data does not name), routeName (readability only), segmentDistanceM (Strava's measured segment length), elapsedSec, avgW (average power over the segment, not the whole activity), weightKg, heightCm, draft (race | solo | ttt - a drafted effort must not be compared against the solo model), frame + wheels + frameLevel (optional, exact catalog names; supplying them turns the check from a +/-2.5% scenario band into a point prediction, and the upgrade level alone is worth ~1.2%), date (game build matters; surfaces change with patches), note

efforts.note: Invented sample row - not a real effort.
Invented sample row, shown with equipment. The real effort on this route is what refuted the sand hypothesis; it lives in the local set, not here.
